focus: Duplicate provisioning: measure the provision_worktree and bun install cost per run in opencode-dual-version.yml, opencode-plugin-tests.yml and hooks-node-tests.yml
answeredQuestions: Which work is duplicated across workflows, and what does the repeated provision_worktree and bun install cost per run?

label: A commit touching .opencode/plugins/**, .skilled/agents/** or .opencode/agents/** starts 5 jobs across opencode-dual-version, opencode-plugin-tests and hooks-node-tests, each running its own actions/checkout and its own provision_worktree: hooks-node-tests' path set is a subset of opencode-plugin-tests' except .hermes/** and the two fired on identical sets of 40 commits with 61 runs each, so hooks-node-tests bought no coverage plugin-tests did not already buy; the four provision steps in the three files are byte-identical apart from their comment.

Median provision_worktree step is 62s per job across 25 sampled jobs (mean 59s, 1480s total), which is exactly the 5 jobs x 5 runs of these three workflows: 63s per hooks run, 64s per plugin-tests run and 173s per dual-version run (v2 67s, v1 56s, both 60s); with the median 51s checkout per job over a 108753-file tree the duplicated floor is 300s provisioning + 255s checkout = 9.3 runner-minutes per commit before any assertion runs, 16 billed minutes against 11 if provision were free.

There is no caching anywhere: across 230 sampled jobs there is no actions/cache step, no cache: input on any of the 35 actions/setup-node invocations, no .github/actions/ composite directory and no workflow_call reusable workflow, so all 14 provisioned trees and 5 built outputs are reinstalled from the network and rebuilt with tsc on every job of every run.

A cache restore of the provisioned trees would move each job below its next billed-minute boundary (-1 min hooks 194->131s, -1 min plugin-tests 138->74s, -3 min dual-version 159/127/137->92/71/77s), i.e. ~145 billed min/day or 3.8% of the 3812 min/day total at 62 runs/day for the pair and 7/day for dual-version, plus ~60s of wall-clock per job.

Merging hooks-node-tests into opencode-plugin-tests is available at no coverage cost: identical triggers and identical provision steps make the merged job 64s provision + 131s hook suites + 74s plugin suites = 269s, 5 billed min against 4+3=7 today, i.e. ~124 billed min/day, and it deletes one checkout (49s) and one provision (63s) per commit; with the cache from f-iter003-004 in place the merged job drops to ~4 billed min, which is why cache and merge belong in one phase (both together ~207 min/day, 5.4%).

Every provision step begins with a per-job network install of the installer itself, npm install --no-save --prefix $RUNNER_TEMP/bun bun@1.3.9, repeated four times in the three workflow files and five times per commit, so that the listed trees that are bun packages can build (the named bun artifact is the sk-vision bundle); the share of the 62s it accounts for is unmeasured and is inferred to be a per-job network constant, which is why the provision step's duration barely tracks how much work a run needs.

The both job of opencode-dual-version provisions before installing two OpenCode versions but only runs the battery, which imports nothing but Node builtins and gives every leg a private mkdtemp data home; because the battery's contract is to prove the plugin folder is discovered, importable and active and the plugins import the gitignored workspace trees, the step is plausibly load-bearing and its 60s x 7 runs/day is UNKNOWN rather than dead work, settleable by dropping the step on a scratch branch and reading whether the plugin leg returns exit 3.

The three workflows' timeouts are ceilings rather than budgets (20/20/30 min against 194/138/159s medians, 6-8x actual), matrix.fail-fast:false is deliberate and correct because the two legs report independently, and none of the three declares concurrency, so a superseded push runs all five jobs to completion and bills for them.

direction: One provisioning job feeding the other four through uploaded build artifacts
reason: Upload happens only after a producer job ends, so four consumers would wait on a full provision plus upload plus download of 14 trees; actions/cache delivers the same bytes to each job without the ordering constraint and without a producer job to keep alive. Rejected on dependency shape, not on size.

direction: Caching node_modules with a key built from package.json alone
reason: The provision path list selects 14 of the repository's package trees and 5 built outputs, so a key from package.json would restore a tree whose lockfile moved underneath it; any key must hash every lockfile under those trees plus worktree-provision-paths.txt so a change in what is provisioned also invalidates the cache.
